title: Universal Depression Screening Protocol with Measurement-Based Care
implementation_guidance: Implement universal depression screening using PHQ-2 for all adult patients; follow positive screens (score ≥3) with PHQ-9 assessment; document scores in structured fields; establish workflow for same-day provider review of positive screens; develop protocol for measurement-based care including standardized follow-up intervals (4-6 weeks initially); use PHQ-9 at each follow-up to track symptom improvement; create registry to monitor patients with positive screens; establish clear referral pathways for severe cases or suicidal ideation; train all staff on screening workflow and documentation.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of depression, enhanced treatment monitoring, better clinical outcomes, reduced symptom severity, increased remission rates, systematic follow-up of diagnosed patients, improved documentation of depression care, reduced missed opportunities for intervention.
target_population: All Medicaid-enrolled adults in primary care settings, with particular attention to those with chronic medical conditions, recent life stressors, or previous history of depression.
citation: Siniscalchi KA, Broome ME, Fish J, et al. Depression screening and measurement-based care in primary care. J Prim Care Community Health. 2020;11:2150132720931261. doi:10.1177/2150132720931261
